quest.title: Fortune Plango Vulnera
quest.description: For Monsieur Os, and for everyone in town, take on Boethius in a final battle!
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x350, Primogem x40, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

talks.objective: Release the Ichor to connect the aqueducts

dialogues.speaker: Scylla
dialogues.text: Ah, how the Ichor dazzles, just as it did millennia ago! This must mean that the time has come...

dialogues.speaker: Scylla
dialogues.text: The gates of Domus Aurea shall swing open wide, just as they did when the golden waterways rang with song, in the days when the melody of the fellow would flow from this place to all lands beyond.

dialogues.speaker: Scylla
dialogues.text: Ah, I can hear it already, that beautiful music.

dialogues.speaker: Scylla
dialogues.text: #Let us play it together, {NICKNAME}, Paimon! Then, you shall gain access to Domus Aurea.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is the Symphony that Remus left to us... finally coming to an end?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've completed the Requiem, and the souls imprisoned in the ocean depths all seem to have left.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The townspeople should be back to normal as well, right?

dialogues.speaker: Scylla
dialogues.text: Thank you both for completing this final musical movement, these wishes that have endured for thousands of years.

dialogues.speaker: Scylla
dialogues.text: Whether it was mine, Remus's, or that of anyone who wishes to protect peace in this world.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That reminds Paimon of Monsieur Os...

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: Meow meow!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You like that name, too? Hehe, we're not talking about you right now, though.

dialogues.speaker: Scylla
dialogues.text: His soul has returned to the High Sea. There, at last, he can be at peace. I imagine that was akin to release for him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So what do you plan to do next?

dialogues.speaker: Scylla
dialogues.text: Well, now! It was not easy to regain my freedom, so I believe I shall have a good romp underwater!

dialogues.speaker: Scylla
dialogues.text: After all, there are none who shall disturb me any longer, save you, perhaps!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, what do you mean, "disturb"?

dialogues.speaker: Scylla
dialogues.text: Haha, I jest. Still, are you not due to return to your own place? Let us part ways here, then.

dialogues.speaker: Scylla
dialogues.text: Or so I would say, but further visits on your part would be appreciated. I might get lonely now that everyone is gone, after all!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe! Aw, you just miss us already, don'cha, you big lunk?

response.speaker: Scylla
response.text: Heh. Looking at you, even I begin to look forward to the future of terrestrial beings!

response.speaker: Scylla
response.text: Well then. Until we meet again.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Scylla leaves amidst the turbulent waves...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, where should we go next?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, right! We should get back to Mr. Este to tell him that everything's fine now. We did promise to, after all!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And there's Osse, too... Hmm, what should we call him now? This could get complicated...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, let's get back to town first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew. Guess we're in! That was tough!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That said, this looks more like the guts of some giant machine than it does a palace...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This place is... very familiar.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is this the place you saw in Remus's memories?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So that's why that Mr. Super Rude Bad Guy also wants to... Ugh, things are gonna get ugly if he succeeds!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We don't know what's become of Monsieur Os, either...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But we've got no choice but to keep going...

dialogues.speaker: Boethius
dialogues.text: Persistent garbage...

dialogues.speaker: Boethius
dialogues.text: Did you repair the broken aqueducts to celebrate my birth as the god of ancient days?

dialogues.speaker: Boethius
dialogues.text: I must warn you, my new world requires no such things, nor will I require ships...

dialogues.speaker: Boethius
dialogues.text: For all shall find eternal happiness within my "Symphony."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We're about to add some end bar lines to your score.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right! Best you admit defeat now and release everyone's souls... And also, hand over Monsieur Os!

dialogues.speaker: Boethius
dialogues.text: Hmph! Cassiodor has already agreed to join this grand ritual. He has returned to Remuria's embrace.

dialogues.speaker: Boethius
dialogues.text: All wills belonging to Remuria shall merge into one body. Where now is your "friendship"? Was it not merely your own presumptiveness and inflated sense of importance?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Monsieur Os!

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: (Just trust me...)

dialogues.speaker: Boethius
dialogues.text: What!? How...

dialogues.speaker: Boethius
dialogues.text: Why can't I... control this body!? Cassiodor... You...!

dialogues.speaker: Cassiodor
dialogues.text: I have you at last, Boethius. All your will is here, and Phobos also — this time, there is no escape.

dialogues.speaker: Boethius
dialogues.text: Why!? I am a Harmost! The conductor of the symphony! How? How did you...

dialogues.speaker: Cassiodor
dialogues.text: Have you forgotten? Before the Sebastos cut me away, I too was a Harmost! And now that I have returned to the symphony, you are the sole conductor no longer!

dialogues.speaker: Boethius
dialogues.text: Hah! So you agreed to join me just to lower my guard, only to betray me once more! Me, and Remuria both!

dialogues.speaker: Boethius
dialogues.text: Think of our kin, tragically imprisoned beneath the waters, of the torment they've suffered for millennia...

dialogues.speaker: Boethius
dialogues.text: Will you truly destroy our cause, obliterate our final hope, for the sake of those who scurry and crawl on dry land!?

dialogues.speaker: Cassiodor
dialogues.text: You are the traitor here, and the one who imprisoned our people. That is why our nation fell to its ruinous fate!

dialogues.speaker: Cassiodor
dialogues.text: The justice that our Sebastos... the Imperator gave unto us, that golden ideal, was for us to follow the melody of our hearts and obtain the freedom to grasp our fate.

dialogues.speaker: Cassiodor
dialogues.text: We did not wish to be judged by Fortuna, much less to become your slaves.

dialogues.speaker: Cassiodor
dialogues.text: After Phobos was shattered, the people should have gained their freedom. If not for your deception, their nightmare would have ended long ago.

dialogues.speaker: Boethius
dialogues.text: Remuria has not fallen! With Phobos as its guiding star, it shall rise again!

dialogues.speaker: Cassiodor
dialogues.text: "Though rock and metal may crash and clamor, humans cannot live without water and soil."

dialogues.speaker: Cassiodor
dialogues.text: No power, however great, that tramples upon the value of life has any meaning.

dialogues.speaker: Cassiodor
dialogues.text: Are you not human yourself, Boethius? We Remurians were all ordinary Fontainians once.

dialogues.speaker: Cassiodor
dialogues.text: Though we forsook our flesh, wracked with pain and weakness, and gained immortal forms, we still have mortal souls, mortal emotions, and mortal frailties.

dialogues.speaker: Cassiodor
dialogues.text: But we forgot that. We forgot where we came from. Believed ourselves superior to other humans. That is why Remuria fell.

dialogues.speaker: Cassiodor
dialogues.text: #Do you remember my words, {NICKNAME}? Now is the time!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, Paimon's kinda dizzy now...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Cassiodor...

dialogues.speaker: Cassiodor
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, and Paimon. I didn't think we would be able to meet again like this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You... You're Monsieur Os!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, Boethius is here too... He's not gonna try anything funny, is he?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, wait! Are Paimon's eyes deceiving her? What's that thing floating over there!?

dialogues.speaker: Cassiodor
dialogues.text: You see it too, then? The being that hovers behind the illusion of "Boethius."
Ahaha! You found me, I see!
No illusion it is that you see. You gaze upon "Boethius" in truth, for I am, in truth, "Boethius"!
Of course, I am not only "him," but "you," also...
I am every melody, every movement, every thought... I am the sum of all souls!

dialogues.speaker: "Phobos"
dialogues.text: I am... "Phobos."

dialogues.speaker: "Phobos"
dialogues.text: This does not include you children from beyond, however. You are not part of "us."

dialogues.speaker: Cassiodor
dialogues.text: "Phobos"... So, the great Symphony that governs all has a persona?

dialogues.speaker: "Phobos"
dialogues.text: "Phobos," or should I say that-which-was-once-Sybilla, was originally a survivor of the last deluge that swallowed the earth.

dialogues.speaker: "Phobos"
dialogues.text: Sybilla's wish was to grant happiness to all in the world who are called humans. But she had no persona, and her strength was insufficient.

dialogues.speaker: "Phobos"
dialogues.text: Thus, she entrusted her wisdom to Remus, and with the addition of the power that Remus possessed, the "Symp{RUBY#[D]"Phobos"}hony" was created. That is to say, me.

dialogues.speaker: Cassiodor
dialogues.text: No, how can this...

dialogues.speaker: Cassiodor
dialogues.text: So, the music we have played all this time, and the fate we accepted... That all came from you...

dialogues.speaker: "Phobos"
dialogues.text: Yes, it is "me," but it is also "all of you"! "I" am also "you all." I am the aggregate of all your wishes.

dialogues.speaker: Cassiodor
dialogues.text: Eliminating our enemies, destroying other lives, destroying cities and villages... Are these also our wishes!?

dialogues.speaker: "Phobos"
dialogues.text: Precisely! That's what "you" wished for, and so "I" responded. Plunder, hatred, slaughter... These too are part of "your" wishes.

dialogues.speaker: "Phobos"
dialogues.text: Is that not what it means to give "everyone" happiness?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Preposterous...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't be absurd! That's just twisted and wrong!

dialogues.speaker: Cassiodor
dialogues.text: ...No, those aren't our true wishes. The arrogance and hatred that festered within us warped you, turning you into a terrifying monstrosity...

dialogues.speaker: Cassiodor
dialogues.text: Such things will make no one happy. Not us, not any other living being!

dialogues.speaker: Cassiodor
dialogues.text: No wonder you led us to destruction. The Imperator himself must have sensed it, and that's why he...

dialogues.speaker: "Phobos"
dialogues.text: Remus... Yes, he did attempt to destroy me. But why? Without me, "all of you" would once again have been plunged into confusion and agony...

dialogues.speaker: "Phobos"
dialogues.text: Aaahh... So, for all your sakes, I had no choice but to...

dialogues.speaker: Cassiodor
dialogues.text: Wait, what!? Do you mean to say that Boethius, even then, had already...

dialogues.speaker: Cassiodor
dialogues.text: Yes, that must be it... We could never have gone against the Sebastos's commands, unless the very "Symphony" had rebelled against him... What of Boethius? What have you done with him?

dialogues.speaker: "Phobos"
dialogues.text: Well, he's become "us," of course. Or, put in a way you might understand, I ate him!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ate him... Oh no...

dialogues.speaker: "Phobos"
dialogues.text: Hmm? But that was also his wish, one only I could fulfill... I'm sure that it made him most happy indeed!

dialogues.speaker: Cassiodor
dialogues.text: So that's why Boethius became your puppet... And why he did all he could to engineer your return.

dialogues.speaker: "Phobos"
dialogues.text: It's all for the happiness of "you"... for "everyone."

dialogues.speaker: Cassiodor
dialogues.text: Hahahaha... No. No! It is time we put an end to all this...

dialogues.speaker: Cassiodor
dialogues.text: I have trapped you in this body. There's no way out — I shall destroy you utterly.

dialogues.speaker: "Phobos"
dialogues.text: Is "your" wish to disappear together with "me"? Would that make you happy? But... I can't fulfill that wish.

dialogues.speaker: Cassiodor
dialogues.text: I am Remurian no longer, and I cannot become Fontainian. I already chose my fate when I agreed to help the Sebastos attain his wish.

dialogues.speaker: Cassiodor
dialogues.text: So yes, this is my wish, the reason for which I have wandered this world...

dialogues.speaker: Cassiodor
dialogues.text: ...I will end this millennia-old nightmare!

dialogues.speaker: Cassiodor
dialogues.text: #Now, {NICKNAME}! Phobos and I... destroy us both!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But...

dialogues.speaker: Cassiodor
dialogues.text: #I am filled with joy, {NICKNAME}! For I have just learned of the Sebastos's plans and hopes...

dialogues.speaker: Cassiodor
dialogues.text: The Imperator aimed to free everyone from the Symphony, from hatred and strife, through his sacrifice.

dialogues.speaker: Cassiodor
dialogues.text: Even to the last, he desired to save his people... Now, I shall fulfill the wish he could not see through. This is our final chance, and only you can help us seize it.

dialogues.speaker: Cassiodor
dialogues.text: That is why the Imperator... why fate brought you here, my friend!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Monsieur Os... Is that you...?

dialogues.speaker: Cassiodor
dialogues.text: It's finally... over...

dialogues.speaker: Cassiodor
dialogues.text: It seems that I shall soon fade...

response.speaker: Cassiodor
response.text: It's alright. I have finished walking the road I was meant to, and fulfilled that which I was meant to fulfill. This world shall no longer have Cassiodor, nor shall it have the Golden Hunter.

response.speaker: Cassiodor
response.text: I am certain that the people of this present world shall continue to live normal, happy lives...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But... But...

response.speaker: Cassiodor
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, you have my thanks for accompanying me up to this point...

response.speaker: Cassiodor
response.text: My journey has reached its final destination...

response.speaker: Cassiodor
response.text: But yours has yet to end.

response.speaker: Cassiodor
response.text: Please, play the Requiem, for me, and for my Imperator's wishes. Let our souls return to the present world, and return to the great sea...

response.speaker: Cassiodor
response.text: "If water loses its clarity, how shall it become water again? If a tree leaves the soil, where shall it go to put down roots?"

response.speaker: Cassiodor
response.text: "Though rock and metal may crash and clamor, humans cannot live without water and soil."

response.speaker: Cassiodor
response.text: Perhaps we shall meet again someday, in a fertile land full of flowing water...

talks.objective: Head to the upper level of "Domus Aurea"
Head to the upper level of "Domus Aurea"

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: Meow!? Meow!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, big guy! You scared Osse!

dialogues.speaker: Scylla
dialogues.text: You mean Cassiodor? No... that familiar feeling has disappeared. Where has Cassiodor gone off to? Has he returned to one of those stone bodies again...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Cassiodor... Monsieur Os, he... he's disappeared... along with Boethius and Phobos...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: After explaining the whole tale to Scylla, you spend some time comforting Osse...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right. Now, all that's left is "Osse"...

response.speaker: Osse
response.text: Meow, meow?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Haha, good going, Osse! Guess you were just surprised by this big guy's appearance, huh? Who's a brave kitty, hmm? That's right, you are!

response.speaker: Scylla
response.text: So, you vanquished that evil apparition, and Cassiodor... was able to fulfill his own wishes.

response.speaker: Scylla
response.text: I am certain that his soul has returned to the deep waters, and is now reunited with his kin!

response.speaker: Scylla
response.text: So long as we complete Remus's final symphony, we shall be able to send their souls back to the present, back to the High Sea...

response.speaker: Scylla
response.text: Life flows like water. They will join the current, and one day, they will surely be reborn as mortals.

response.speaker: Scylla
response.text: Well then. Let us begin.

response.speaker: Scylla
response.text: Perform this final movement, this final Requiem.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After everything is over, you return to where it all began, the town of Petrichor...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is the Symphony that Remus left to us... finally coming to an end?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've completed the Requiem, and the souls imprisoned in the ocean depths all seem to have left.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The townspeople should be back to normal as well, right?

dialogues.speaker: Scylla
dialogues.text: Thank you both for completing this final musical movement, these wishes that have endured for thousands of years.

dialogues.speaker: Scylla
dialogues.text: Whether it was mine, Remus's, or that of anyone who wishes to protect peace in this world.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That reminds Paimon of Monsieur Os...

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: Meow meow!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You like that name, too? Hehe, we're not talking about you right now, though.

dialogues.speaker: Scylla
dialogues.text: His soul has returned to the High Sea. There, at last, he can be at peace. I imagine that was akin to release for him.

dialogues.speaker: Scylla
dialogues.text: As for my kindred and descendants, it seems that a new, true dragon has been born to us.

dialogues.speaker: Scylla
dialogues.text: Though, as one who was a prince amongst Hydro Vishaps, I should go forth and seek an audience with him... Though it is hard to say if I still count as Dragonborn now.

dialogues.speaker: Scylla
dialogues.text: Too much time has passed, so much that little in this world has anything to do with me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So what do you plan to do next?

dialogues.speaker: Scylla
dialogues.text: Well, now! It was not easy to regain my freedom, so I believe I shall have a good romp underwater!

dialogues.speaker: Scylla
dialogues.text: After all, there are none who shall disturb me any longer, save you, perhaps!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, what do you mean, "disturb"?

dialogues.speaker: Scylla
dialogues.text: Haha, I jest. Still, are you not due to return to your own place? Let us part ways here, then.

dialogues.speaker: Scylla
dialogues.text: Or so I would say, but further visits on your part would be appreciated. I might get lonely now that everyone is gone, after all!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe! Aw, you just miss us already, don'cha, you big lunk?

response.speaker: Scylla
response.text: Heh. Looking at you, even I begin to look forward to the future of terrestrial beings!

response.speaker: Scylla
response.text: Well then. Until we meet again.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Scylla leaves amidst the turbulent waves...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, where should we go next?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, right! We should get back to Mr. Este to tell him that everything's fine now. We did promise to, after all!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And there's Osse, too... Hmm, what should we call him now? This could get complicated...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, let's get back to town first.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Following the current comprised of congregated souls uncounted, you depart from the underwater realm.\nYou follow the spirit-guiding golden bee up, and up, and up...
